items.question: What is the biggest benefit of hiring a Master Elite contractor?

items.question: Is Golden Pledge automatically included with every Roof King roof?

children.text: Product coverage concerns manufacturing defects. Misapplication coverage concerns covered installation errors. Golden Pledge includes both, with the covered products, flashings, remedies and conditions defined in its written terms.

editorial.title: Siding replacement cost in Cincinnati, OH
editorial.description: What drives siding replacement cost in Cincinnati: wall area, material, removal, repairs and trim, with a dated national benchmark and city permit guidance.
editorial.focus: Choose a roofing or storm restoration service, or begin a siding project with its material and installation details in view.

hero.title: Siding replacement cost in Cincinnati, OH
hero.description: Siding replacement cost in Cincinnati comes down to wall area, material, removal and what is found underneath. Consumer Reports, citing the 2025 Cost vs. Value report, gives national averages of nearly $18,000 for vinyl and above $21,000 for fiber cement. Those are national benchmarks, not Cincinnati prices or Roof King quotes. Your price comes from measuring your walls and itemizing the work.

faq.title: Siding cost questions for Cincinnati homeowners

items.question: How much does siding replacement cost in Cincinnati?

children.text: Consumer Reports cites national averages of nearly $18,000 for vinyl and above $21,000 for fiber cement, based on the 2025 Cost vs. Value report. These are not Cincinnati prices or Roof King quotes. A measured estimate prices your walls, materials, removal and repairs.

items.question: Do I need a siding permit in Cincinnati?

children.text: Generally not for replacement siding on a one-, two- or three-family detached dwelling inside city limits, under the city guide. Historic properties, different building types and other jurisdictions need separate checks.

items.question: What changes in a Cincinnati historic district?

children.text: A Certificate of Appropriateness may be needed even when a building permit is not. District guidelines can affect material, profile and color. Get the required approval before ordering.

items.question: Is replacing one elevation cheaper?

children.text: The total is often lower because there is less wall to replace. Matching faded or discontinued panels is the trade-off. Compare new samples against the existing walls.

items.question: Does removal add to the price?

children.text: Yes. Layers, haul-away and disposal affect the total. Agree how repairs to exposed sheathing and flashing are documented, priced and approved.

items.question: Can I price siding from floor area?

children.text: No. Floor area does not measure gables, tall walls, additions and openings. Measure each exterior elevation and the detail work around it.

items.question: Can I finance the project?

children.text: Three- and five-year options, with payments as low as $47 on qualifying projects, are available subject to lender approval and applicable terms. Compare financing separately from the project price.

sections.title: Compare siding materials and installation costs

children.text: Vinyl profiles and finishes have their own accessory and attachment systems. Compare the selected panel, corner and opening details, and whether a particular insulation component is included. Standard vinyl and insulated products should not be treated as the same specification.

Engineered wood combines a wood-based siding appearance with product-specific finishing and installation requirements. The estimate needs to identify the finish, trim and treatment of cut edges and connections for the chosen product.

Fiber cement offers different profiles and finish choices, with its own handling, fastening and detailing requirements. Compare the complete installation rather than assuming a material category comes with one universal price. The
siding materials guide
explains these options further.

sections.title: What adds to a siding replacement quote?

cards.title: Old siding removal and concealed wall repairs

children.text: Removal exposes the wall beneath the old siding. Deteriorated sheathing or trim, unresolved water entry and incomplete flashing may need attention before the new finish is installed. Ask how those findings will be photographed, priced and approved. A new panel cannot correct a concealed wall problem that remains untreated.

cards.title: Window trim, corners, soffits and fixtures

children.text: Corners, window and door trim, roof-to-wall transitions, soffit or fascia work, fixture removal and reinstallation, and cleanup all affect the work. Identify what is included and what will remain. If painting or gutter work is separate, record the boundary and sequence so the finished exterior is coordinated.

cards.title: Like-for-like siding or a redesigned exterior

children.text: A like-for-like replacement with limited trim changes differs from a project that introduces new accent areas, extensive opening details or wall repairs. Both may cover similar wall areas. The useful comparison lists the material, preparation and finish work before the total. Approved measured pricing is needed to turn either approach into a project budget.

expectedBlocks: Siding replacement cost in Cincinnati comes down to wall area, material, removal and what is found underneath. Consumer Reports, citing the 2025 Cost vs. Value report, gives national averages of nearly $18,000 for vinyl and above $21,000 for fiber cement. Those are national benchmarks, not Cincinnati prices or Roof King quotes. Your price comes from measuring your walls and itemizing the work.

Vinyl profiles and finishes have their own accessory and attachment systems. Compare the selected panel, corner and opening details, and whether a particular insulation component is included. Standard vinyl and insulated products should not be treated as the same specification.

Engineered wood combines a wood-based siding appearance with product-specific finishing and installation requirements. The estimate needs to identify the finish, trim and treatment of cut edges and connections for the chosen product.

Fiber cement offers different profiles and finish choices, with its own handling, fastening and detailing requirements. Compare the complete installation rather than assuming a material category comes with one universal price. The siding materials guide explains these options further.

Removal exposes the wall beneath the old siding. Deteriorated sheathing or trim, unresolved water entry and incomplete flashing may need attention before the new finish is installed. Ask how those findings will be photographed, priced and approved. A new panel cannot correct a concealed wall problem that remains untreated.

Corners, window and door trim, roof-to-wall transitions, soffit or fascia work, fixture removal and reinstallation, and cleanup all affect the work. Identify what is included and what will remain. If painting or gutter work is separate, record the boundary and sequence so the finished exterior is coordinated.

A like-for-like replacement with limited trim changes differs from a project that introduces new accent areas, extensive opening details or wall repairs. Both may cover similar wall areas. The useful comparison lists the material, preparation and finish work before the total. Approved measured pricing is needed to turn either approach into a project budget.

items.question: Do I need a permit to replace siding in Columbus?

children.text: Yes, inside city limits. Columbus requires a building permit to replace exterior siding but not plan review. Special districts can need further approval; neighboring cities and townships apply their own rules.

items.question: Is full replacement needed for one damaged area?

children.text: Not automatically. The cause, condition of the surrounding wall and availability of matching material determine whether a focused repair is practical.

items.question: Does new siding fix a wall leak?

children.text: Only if the source is found and repaired. Flashing, the weather barrier or a window or roof connection may be the cause. New cladding should not hide it.

items.question: Does the workmanship warranty cover siding?

sections.title: How we assess siding damage

children.text: An inspection separates damage to the siding from a problem behind it. These are the three areas we check.
Call for an inspection when you notice:
Buckled, warped or loose courses, or panels that have slipped out of place
Cracks, holes or broken corners after hail or impact
Exposed housewrap or sheathing where a panel is missing
Staining, soft trim or peeling paint near openings
Gaps at corners or where siding meets the roof
Uneven fading and patches that no longer match
Some signs involve the panel itself; staining near a window can start with failed flashing behind it. The inspection is about finding which.

cards.title: Checking flashing and moisture behind siding

faq.title: Siding replacement questions

items.question: Do I need a permit to replace siding in Columbus?

children.text: Yes, inside city limits. Columbus lists replacement siding as requiring a building permit without plan review. State who applies in the agreement; other jurisdictions set their own requirements.

items.question: Can you replace siding on one side of the house?

children.text: Often. End new work at a corner, trim board or material change. A matching color name may still look different beside aged panels, so compare samples outside.

items.question: How long does siding replacement take?

children.text: Wall area, stories, layers to remove, hidden damage and weather all affect the sequence. Define the product and repairs before setting the expected schedule.

items.question: Will new siding lower energy bills?

children.text: That depends on the installed assembly. Insulated vinyl or a separate insulation layer changes the wall differently from a standard siding panel. Name the actual product and documented insulation value in the estimate.

items.question: Does insurance pay for storm-damaged siding?

children.text: Coverage depends on your policy and the insurer’s findings. Roof King documents the siding, trim and roof edge for the repair discussion.
Storm damage documentation

items.question: What does the workmanship warranty cover?

children.text: Our 5-year workmanship warranty covers installation under the written project terms. Product defects are addressed by the manufacturer’s warranty; storm damage is considered separately.

items.question: Can I finance siding replacement?

children.text: Three- and five-year options are available, with payments as low as $47 on qualifying projects. Financing is subject to lender approval and applicable terms. Compare the cash price, APR, fees and total repayment.

sections.title: How the wall is prepared for new siding

children.text: Removal exposes the wall and connections the new cladding will depend on.

Old siding can hide soft sheathing, deteriorated trim and gaps in the weather barrier, especially below windows and near the base of walls. Record findings, obtain approval for the repair price and correct damaged components before the wall is covered again.

Water behind siding must be directed outside. Lap the barrier and integrate window and door flashing so water sheds over it rather than behind it. New cladding alone does not fix a leaking opening; identify any separate window or door repair in the estimate.

Where siding meets a lower roof, masonry or a deck, the connection needs appropriate flashing and the selected product’s clearances. Sealant alone cannot replace these details. Coordinate roofing and cladding before either covers the connection.

items.question: What is the best type of siding for a Columbus home?

children.text: Compare your priorities: vinyl for finished color and relatively low upkeep, LP SmartSide for engineered-wood profiles and finishes, and James Hardie for rigid fiber cement and architectural profiles. All need correct barrier and flashing details.

items.question: Is insulated vinyl the same as standard vinyl?

children.text: Consider the complete assembly, installation, maintenance and written coverage as well as any life estimate. A generic category claim does not establish how long a particular roof will serve your home.

items.question: Can I change materials during replacement?

children.text: Possibly. The new system needs to suit the roof and supporting construction. Identify preparation, attachment, weight and connection requirements in the assessment before committing to the change.

items.question: Do warranties cover the installation as well as the product?

children.text: That depends on the specific documents and eligibility. Manufacturer product or system coverage and contractor workmanship terms should be reviewed separately.

children.text: The sloped roof surface is different from the living area below it. Overhangs, garages, additions and roof geometry affect the measurement. Roofing estimates may use squares, where one square equals 100 square feet of roof area. Material ordering also accounts for the layout and cutting requirements; it is not simply the measured area converted directly into packages.

For illustration, 2,000 square feet of measured roof surface equals 20 roofing squares before ordering allowances. That arithmetic does not establish a price, material order or the condition of the roof. A property with the same living area can have a substantially different roof surface.

expectedBlocks: The cost of a replacement roof depends on the roof and the work beneath the new covering. Roof King prepares project estimates around measured areas, selected materials, access and the condition of the existing assembly. This guide explains the items to compare before deciding whether two prices describe the same job.
Roof area, roofing squares and replacement cost
Measuring the sloped roof surface, including garages and additions

The sloped roof surface is different from the living area below it. Overhangs, garages, additions and roof geometry affect the measurement. Roofing estimates may use squares, where one square equals 100 square feet of roof area. Material ordering also accounts for the layout and cutting requirements; it is not simply the measured area converted directly into packages.

For illustration, 2,000 square feet of measured roof surface equals 20 roofing squares before ordering allowances. That arithmetic does not establish a price, material order or the condition of the roof. A property with the same living area can have a substantially different roof surface.
What changes the price of a Columbus roof replacement
Roof shape and access
Steep slopes, height, valleys, dormers and limited access affect how the work is carried out. Two equal roof areas can require different labor and connection details.
Removal and the supporting surface

The existing covering, number of layers and disposal requirements affect preparation. Damaged decking found after tear-off adds a separate decision. The estimate should state how that work is documented, priced and authorized.
Covering and accessories

Compare the actual shingle or metal system, underlayment, edge details, flashing and ventilation work. A material upgrade can change companion components as well as the visible covering. The roofing product library is a starting point for exact selections.
Why similar-size roofs can have different replacement costs
A straightforward roof replacement

A simple roof with accessible staging, limited intersections and serviceable decking still needs removal, preparation, specified components and cleanup. Its estimate should list those items even when there are fewer construction details to resolve.
A roof with more connections and concealed work

A similarly sized roof with several valleys, wall intersections or deteriorated decking needs additional preparation and detailing. The difference is not explained by shingle area alone. These examples illustrate differences in included materials and repairs; they are not Roof King jobs or price quotations.

Changing a shingle profile or moving from shingles to metal can alter the accessories, attachment and finishing details as well as the covering price. Compare both options against the same roof measurements, removal work and repair allowances to see what the material change actually adds.

Ask whether decking, flashing replacement, ventilation changes, permits where applicable, disposal and cleanup are included or treated separately. Why do two estimates differ?

They may use different materials, preparation, allowances, exclusions or coverage. Align the work before comparing totals. A lower number may describe less work, while a higher number still needs a clear explanation.

Where a Dublin roof meets retained brick or siding, the replacement needs a coordinated wall-side connection. Identify adjoining repairs before new shingles conceal the transition.

Attic and roof ventilation should be evaluated with the installation. The relevant product requirements and actual roof conditions determine the work; ventilation is not simply an accessory to add without considering the existing arrangement.

faq.title: Commercial roofing questions

items.question: Can a commercial roof leak be repaired without replacing the entire roof?

children.text: Sometimes. The cause and extent of damage, existing roof system, surrounding material and concealed conditions determine whether a localized repair is reasonable. A proposal should explain what the repair addresses and what remains unchanged.

items.question: Does a commercial roofing estimate include drainage corrections?

children.text: Not automatically. Ask whether the proposed work addresses drains, scuppers, gutters, slopes and discharge connections, or only the roof covering. Any necessary drainage changes should be identified in writing.

items.question: Can tenants remain in the building during roofing work?

children.text: That depends on the work, building use, access and safety requirements. Discuss tenant entrances, delivery schedules, equipment and sensitive areas before scheduling. The plan should describe expected restrictions rather than guarantee zero disruption.

items.question: Which commercial roof material is best for my building?

children.text: There is no single answer for every property. The existing construction, slope, drainage, rooftop equipment, installation requirements and budget all matter. Compare written proposals for complete assemblies rather than choosing by membrane name alone.

items.question: Does a workmanship warranty cover the roofing material too?

children.text: Workmanship coverage and manufacturer product coverage are different. Request the written terms that apply to the specific commercial project and verify any system-specific qualification or warranty requirements.

items.question: What if storm damage is involved?

children.text: Document affected areas safely, note interior water entry and preserve prior roof records. The roofing assessment should separate observed conditions from proposed work. Insurance coverage and payment decisions belong to the insurer; a roofing estimate is not a coverage guarantee.

sections.title: What a Commercial Roof Assessment Should Examine

children.text: A building may have a single low-slope roof, multiple sections with different ages, or sloped areas that meet membrane roofing. Inspect the assembly and its connections before deciding which work is appropriate.

The inspection should distinguish the general roof surface from transitions where materials meet: membrane seams, roof edges, skylights, vents, equipment curbs, wall flashings and other penetrations. A visible split or lifted component can indicate a repair location, but the surrounding condition determines whether the proposed work is sufficient.

cards.title: Drainage and the Route Water Takes

children.text: Discuss roof slopes, low spots, outlets, scuppers, gutters and downspouts. Ask whether a proposed repair or replacement will correct a drainage concern or only renew the roof covering. Persistent ponding or repeated overflow should be evaluated rather than treated as a cosmetic issue.

The visible surface does not reveal every condition below it. Previous leaks may have affected insulation or other components. A written proposal should state which conditions have been confirmed, which remain uncertain, and how additional work will be evaluated and approved after removal begins.

HVAC units, exhaust equipment, service paths and attached fixtures can complicate roof work. Establish which connections the roofing work includes and which require another contractor. The project plan should account for equipment access rather than assume every unit can remain accessible at all times.

Consider the location and frequency of leaks, repair history, material condition, evidence of moisture beneath the surface, drainage and the remaining serviceability of the assembly. An isolated detail on an otherwise sound roof can lead to a different recommendation than widespread deterioration.

Coatings or recover approaches should not be assumed suitable for every existing roof. Their appropriateness depends on the assembly, substrate condition, moisture, applicable requirements and the actual products proposed. Ask what investigation supports the recommendation and what it resolves.

children.text: Overflowing gutters are easy to ignore until water starts running across an entrance, down an exterior wall or toward the foundation. On a commercial building, those problems can affect tenants, deliveries and the condition of the property.

Roof King & Restoration provides commercial gutter installation, replacement and repair in the Columbus area. We assess the roof area feeding the gutter and follow the water through the outlet and downspout to its discharge point.

sections.title: Why Commercial Gutters Overflow

children.text: Leaves, roof debris and sediment can collect at outlets. If water can't leave the gutter, it may spill over the front or back. An outlet can also appear clear while the restriction is farther down the downspout or beyond the building.

Some roof areas send a large volume of water to one point. Increasing the gutter size alone may not help if the outlets and downspouts still restrict the flow. The complete drainage route needs to be considered.

cards.title: Water Discharged in the Wrong Place

children.text: A functioning gutter can still leave water beside a foundation, across a walkway or near a loading area if the downspout terminates poorly. Underground drainage and site grading may need attention from the appropriate trade. The gutter estimate should make clear where Roof King's work ends.

Sagging gutters, loose attachments, deteriorated fascia and damaged edge metal can change the gutter's slope or allow water behind it. Supporting repairs should be identified before the new gutter is installed.

sections.title: Gutters, Scuppers and Internal Roof Drains

children.text: Not every commercial roof uses an external gutter. Some low-slope roofs rely on scuppers through parapet walls, internal drains or a combination of systems. These components carry water differently and may connect to separate piping or site drainage.

Before replacing an external gutter, identify whether the problem begins on the roof, at the outlet or farther downstream. A blocked internal drain or underground line needs its own diagnosis. Replacing an external gutter only helps if that gutter is causing the problem.

Roof King's commercial roofing team can discuss the roof-to-gutter connection. Work involving internal piping, underground drainage or grading should be identified separately when it is outside the gutter work.

children.text: Commercial gutters come in different materials, shapes and sizes. The appropriate choice depends on the roof area, building design, exposure and how the gutter will be supported. A proposal should name the actual material, finish, profile and attachment method rather than rely on a generic description.
Gutter guards may help limit the debris entering a system, but they do not eliminate inspections or maintenance.
Guards also have to suit the gutter, roof edge and expected debris. We assess compatibility with the proposed gutter and roof edge before recommending a protection product.
If a seamless gutter configuration is appropriate, we can discuss it in relation to the building's roofline and outlet locations.

sections.title: Planning Gutter Work Around an Occupied Building

children.text: Commercial gutter installation often requires lifts, ladders, material staging and temporary access restrictions. That can affect storefront entrances, loading docks, parking spaces and service areas.

Before scheduling, we need to understand where people enter the building, when deliveries occur and whether other exterior work is planned. If the roofing, siding or fascia also needs attention, the order of work matters. The written proposal should identify which contractor handles each connection and what access the property must provide.
Discuss temporary restrictions with tenants and staff before work starts. The available sequence depends on the equipment, building access and repairs involved.

children.text: The exact gutter runs, elevations, outlets and downspouts included in the work.
Proposed gutter material, size, profile, finish and attachment details.
Removal and disposal of existing components, where applicable.
Required repairs to fascia, edge metal or supporting construction.
Discharge locations and any drainage work specifically excluded.

faq.title: Commercial roof repair questions

items.question: Can you repair a TPO or EPDM roof without replacing it?

children.text: Sometimes. Localized damage to a TPO or EPDM roof may be repairable if the surrounding materials and underlying assembly remain suitable. The repair needs materials and methods compatible with the existing system.

items.question: How do you find a leak when the ceiling stain is far from the damage?

children.text: An assessment considers the leak history and roof details such as seams, equipment curbs, flashings and drainage paths. Water can travel before becoming visible indoors, so the ceiling stain is a starting clue rather than proof of the entry point.

items.question: Can commercial roof repairs be completed while tenants are inside?

children.text: That depends on the work, roof access, building operations and safety requirements. Discuss entrances, equipment, sensitive areas and operating hours before scheduling.

items.question: Will a repair affect my existing roof warranty?

children.text: It might. Manufacturer warranties can include specific materials, installer qualifications and notice requirements. Review the existing documents before authorizing work; do not assume every repair preserves coverage.

items.question: What should a commercial roof repair estimate include?

children.text: Look for the affected roof area, observed condition, proposed repair materials, preparation, adjoining flashing and drainage work, cleanup, exclusions and a process for approving concealed-condition changes.

items.question: When should I consider replacing the commercial roof instead?

children.text: A replacement assessment may be appropriate when leaks recur across different areas, the roof covering is broadly deteriorated or concealed damage makes isolated repairs impractical. Compare the documented findings and proposed work rather than deciding based on one leak alone.

sections.title: Commercial Roof Systems We Offer

children.text: Different buildings call for different roofing materials. Roof King offers Mule-Hide TPO and EPDM systems as well as commercial metal roofing. The right choice depends on the existing construction, roof slope, drainage, rooftop equipment and the details required for installation.
For a closer look at the materials, visit our
commercial roof types
page.

TPO is a single-ply roofing membrane used on many low-slope commercial buildings. It offers a light-colored roof surface and heat-welded seams. The details matter as much as the membrane itself: insulation, attachment, flashing, edges and drains all need to work together. We’ll specify those components in the proposed work rather than give you a price based only on square footage.

EPDM is a flexible rubber membrane commonly used on low-slope roofs. It has different seam and flashing requirements than TPO, and the condition of the existing roof affects how a replacement should be designed. We’ll review the substrate, insulation, roof edges and penetrations before selecting an assembly.

Metal roofing can be a good fit for certain commercial buildings, particularly where the roof design and slope suit a metal system. Panel selection, fastening, underlayment, flashing and transitions around equipment need to be addressed in the proposal. Metal isn’t the right answer for every low-slope roof, and we won’t present it that way.

sections.title: What Happens to the Existing Roof?

cards.title: Tear-Off, Insulation Removal and Concealed Repairs

children.text: A full tear-off allows the crew to remove the specified roofing layers and inspect conditions that aren’t visible from the surface. Wet insulation, deteriorated decking and earlier repairs may change what the building needs. The estimate should explain what is included in removal and how additional work will be handled if concealed damage is found.

cards.title: Recover Suitability and the Retained Roof

children.text: In some cases, a new roof can be installed over the existing assembly. That decision requires more than a visual inspection. Existing moisture, roof layers, structural loading, material compatibility and local code requirements all matter. If a recover approach is appropriate, the proposal should explain why.

A replacement is also the time to address problems that may have contributed to the old roof’s failure. That can include wet insulation, low areas that hold water, deteriorated edge details or drains that aren’t functioning as intended. We’ll identify which of those items are part of the proposed work and which need further investigation.

Commercial roofs have more vulnerable connections than most people realize. HVAC curbs, exhaust vents, skylights, parapet walls, internal drains and roof edges all interrupt the main roofing surface. Those areas need to be included in the replacement plan.

Before work starts, the work should make clear whether rooftop equipment must be moved, who is responsible for disconnecting and reconnecting it, and how new roofing will tie into the surrounding components. Drainage also needs its own review. A new membrane won’t solve a roof that still sends water to the wrong place.
If gutters or exterior drainage are part of the problem, see our commercial gutters and drainage page.

sections.title: How We Plan a Commercial Roof Replacement

cards.title: Review the Building and Roof History

children.text: We start with what’s known: roof age, past repairs, leak locations, existing documents and any areas that are difficult to access. We also need to understand how the building operates. A warehouse with scheduled deliveries has different requirements than an occupied office or a multi-tenant retail property.

The proposal should identify the roof sections being replaced, the selected roofing system, tear-off or recover work, insulation, flashings, drainage, cleanup and exclusions. If there are conditions that can’t be confirmed until removal begins, those should be explained up front.

cards.title: Coordinate the Work Around the Property

children.text: Roofing work affects access, parking, deliveries and sometimes rooftop mechanical equipment. We’ll discuss those constraints before scheduling so the owner or property manager knows what to expect. Some disruption may be unavoidable, but it should not come as a surprise.

If concealed damage is found, the work and cost of additional work should be documented and approved. At the end of the project, keep the final work description, product information, applicable inspection records and written warranty documents together with the building’s maintenance records.

sections.title: Comparing Commercial Roof Replacement Estimates

children.text: Two bids can look similar at the bottom line and describe very different projects. Before choosing a contractor, compare the actual work included.
Which roof sections and existing layers are being removed or retained?
What specific TPO, EPDM or metal assembly is proposed?
Are insulation, flashing, drains and perimeter details included?
How will rooftop equipment and occupied areas be handled?
What happens if damaged decking or wet insulation is uncovered?
Who is responsible for permits, inspections and cleanup?
What written workmanship and manufacturer warranty terms apply?
A clear estimate makes it easier to understand the price and avoids disagreements over work that one contractor included and another left out.

cards.title: Replacing a Roof After Storm Damage

children.text: High winds, hail and debris can damage membranes, metal panels, flashings and rooftop equipment. If a storm has caused leaks, photograph the damage from safe locations and keep records of when the problems appeared. Do not send employees onto a damaged roof to investigate.

Our commercial storm damage page covers storm-related inspections and documentation in more detail. A roofing estimate describes the work needed; it does not determine whether an insurance company will cover the loss.

children.text: TPO, EPDM and metal roofing all have a place on commercial buildings. They aren't interchangeable, though, and choosing one starts with understanding the building—not picking a material from a brochure.

Roof King & Restoration works with Columbus-area property owners on commercial roofing projects. We offer Mule-Hide TPO and EPDM roofing products, along with commercial metal roofing. If you're planning a replacement or trying to identify the roof already on your building, we'll review the existing conditions and explain which options make sense for the work.

sections.title: Compare TPO, EPDM and Metal Roofing

children.text: TPO (thermoplastic polyolefin) is a single-ply membrane used on flat and low-slope commercial roofs. The membrane sheets are joined with heat-welded seams. TPO is often selected when a building owner wants a light-colored roofing surface, but color alone is not a reason to choose it.

A TPO proposal needs to describe the entire assembly: existing roof preparation, insulation or cover board, how the membrane is attached, seams, flashing, perimeter edges and drainage connections. Roof penetrations and HVAC curbs deserve particular attention. Those details determine how the installed roof works as a system.
Roof King offers Mule-Hide TPO products. The specific product and installation method should be named in the written proposal.

EPDM (ethylene propylene diene monomer) is a synthetic-rubber membrane used on many low-slope commercial buildings. Unlike TPO, EPDM seams rely on system-specific tapes, primers and adhesives rather than heat welding.
Repairs and new installation require products compatible with the membrane.

An EPDM roof should be evaluated at seams, walls, drains, penetrations and perimeter details—not just in the middle of the roof. When replacing an older assembly, the condition of the insulation and deck also affects what can remain in place.
Roof King offers Mule-Hide EPDM products. We'll discuss whether EPDM fits your building's roof layout and project requirements.

Metal roofing is an option for commercial buildings with suitable roof geometry and slope. The panel type, fastening method, underlayment, transitions and flashing all matter. A roof with numerous equipment penetrations or complicated intersections needs careful detailing.

Metal roofing isn't a substitute for a low-slope membrane on every building. We review the structure, drainage and existing construction before recommending it. The estimate should identify the metal system being proposed rather than refer to 'metal roofing' as if all panels perform the same way.

cards.title: What If Your Building Has Another Roof Type?

children.text: Some Columbus commercial buildings have modified bitumen, built-up asphalt roofing, older membranes or steep-slope shingles. Those systems may be present on a building even though they aren't among the three commercial products Roof King has confirmed offering for new installation.

If you're unsure what is on your roof, don't guess from a photograph or the surface color. Roof records, visible details and an on-site assessment can help identify the material and determine whether a compatible repair is practical.
We'll discuss the work Roof King can perform on your specific building; we won't describe an unconfirmed product as one we install.

TPO and EPDM are commonly used on low-slope roofs. Metal roofing depends on the particular panel system and roof configuration. A building with both low-slope and pitched sections may need more than one roofing approach, with carefully planned transitions between them.

cards.title: Choosing a System for an Occupied Commercial Building

children.text: Commercial roofing work often takes place while a business is operating. Before a material is selected, we need to know how the building is used. Roof access, tenant entrances, deliveries, equipment service and areas sensitive to noise or dust can affect the installation plan.

A warehouse with rooftop units and regular truck traffic presents different logistical issues than a small office or retail building. The work should address those conditions, including any work that needs to be coordinated with other trades. Not every interruption can be avoided, but it should be discussed before construction begins.

sections.caption: Illustration of related components. Materials and details vary with the selected system.

sections.title: Commercial Roof Assemblies: Covering, Insulation and Connections

children.text: The visible roof covering is only one part of the assembly. The deck supports the system. Insulation and cover boards may serve thermal, protective and attachment functions. Fasteners or adhesives secure the materials.
Flashing completes the transitions at walls, curbs and penetrations.

Those layers matter most when a roof is being replaced. If water has reached the insulation or the deck has deteriorated, putting a new membrane over the problem may leave the owner with the same underlying issue. We look at what is known, what needs further investigation and what the proposed work actually includes.

cards.title: Membrane Seams and Compatible Repair Materials

children.text: TPO seams are heat welded; EPDM seams use compatible tapes and adhesives. Metal roofs have panel joints, fasteners or clips, and flashing connections. A repair needs to match the actual system on the roof. Using the wrong materials can turn a small problem into a recurring leak.

cards.title: Parapets, Equipment Curbs and Drainage Outlets

children.text: A membrane or panel does not correct poor drainage by itself. We look at where water collects, how it reaches drains or gutters, and what happens around equipment curbs, parapet walls and roof edges. If the roof has a persistent drainage issue, that should be part of the project discussion.
Consider the roof outlets together with
commercial gutters
and discharge routes.

sections.title: What to Ask Before Approving a Commercial Roof Proposal

children.text: What roof system is currently installed, and how was it identified?
Which Mule-Hide TPO, Mule-Hide EPDM or metal products are being proposed?
What existing layers will be removed, repaired or left in place?
Are insulation, flashing, drains, gutters and perimeter details included?
Who handles work around HVAC units, skylights and other rooftop equipment?
How will additional damage discovered during removal be documented and approved?
Which written workmanship and manufacturer documents apply to this project?
Two estimates can use the same material name while including very different amounts of preparation and detail work.

cards.title: Repair, Replacement or a Different Approach?

children.text: A roof leak doesn't automatically call for a replacement. If the membrane is generally sound and the damage is confined to a flashing or seam, a repair may be appropriate. Repeated leaks, widespread deterioration or moisture beneath the surface can change that decision.

Roof coatings and recover installations are sometimes discussed for older commercial roofs. They are not universal fixes. Their suitability depends on the existing assembly, moisture conditions, product compatibility and applicable requirements. Roof King should confirm whether either approach is available and appropriate before it appears in a proposal.
For leak-specific work, see
commercial roof repair
. For a full reroofing project, review
commercial roof replacement

Ask for a proposal that identifies the actual roofing products and assembly. Manufacturer product coverage and a contractor's workmanship coverage are separate. The documents available for a commercial job depend on the system, project and applicable terms; don't assume a warranty based on the material name.

opening.title: Storm Damage Help, From the First Hour to the Finished Roof
opening.description: Start with the tab that matches where you are. Managing a business or multifamily building? Explore commercial storm damage.

items.title: Right after the storm

children.text: Safety comes first. Then slow down any water coming in, and only then start recording what happened. None of it requires you to go on the roof.

items.description: Safety comes first. Then slow down any water coming in, and only then start recording what happened. None of it requires you to go on the roof.
items.label: Explore Storm Damage Documentation

cards.title: Stay off the roof and clear of hazards
cards.description: Damage you can see from the ground is enough to start with. Don't climb up or pull at loose material.

children.text: Stay out of rooms with sagging or soaked ceilings, and out of any building with visible structural damage until a professional clears it . If you smell gas, leave right away and call Columbia Gas from outside . Downed power lines are a 911 call . Don't use wet electrical equipment until a licensed electrician has checked it . Run a generator outdoors only, at least 20 feet from the house .

cards.title: Slow the water down
cards.description: Temporary protection limits damage while the permanent repair is planned. It doesn't replace the repair.

children.text: Move belongings out of the way, catch drips and start drying wet materials within 24 to 48 hours to limit mold . If water is coming through the roof, call (614) 379-8893. Call Roof King to discuss temporary protection and inspection availability . Keep receipts for tarps, buckets, fans and any temporary repairs . Ask what the tarp covers and what permanent work is still needed.

cards.title: Photograph before you clean up
cards.description: Your own dated photos and video are the first part of the storm record.

children.text: Walk all four sides of the house and take wide shots from the ground, then close-ups of shingles in the yard, gutters, siding, screens and windows . Inside, photograph ceiling stains, wet insulation you can see from the attic hatch, and damaged belongings . Note the date and time of the storm and when you first noticed each problem. Don't throw out damaged items until your insurer says you can .

cards.title: Report the damage to your insurer yourself
cards.description: Policies can have reporting deadlines, so contact your insurer promptly and ask what records it needs .

children.text: Keep your policy number handy . Calling a roofer does not start a claim, and Roof King does not file one on your behalf . The
insurance claims tab
explains who does what.

cards.title: Find the storm date
cards.description: The storm report lists NOAA hail and wind reports near your address since 2019 .

children.text: These are reports, not a record of every hailstone. Hail falls in narrow bands, so a quiet result doesn't prove your roof is fine, and a nearby report doesn't prove it was hit . What the report gives you is a likely date.

image.alt: Supplied photograph of a shingle roof above a porch and adjoining exterior

items.caption: Residential exterior photograph supplied by Roof King; location is not asserted.

items.title: What damage to look for

children.text: Storm damage rarely stops at the shingles. Here is what to look for on each part of the house, and which parts only show up when someone inspects the roof itself.

items.description: Storm damage rarely stops at the shingles. Here is what to look for on each part of the house, and which parts only show up when someone inspects the roof itself.
items.label: Explore Storm Damage Documentation

groups.title: What damage to look for — Details

cards.title: Shingles
cards.description: Missing, lifted or creased shingles after wind; bruising, cracks or exposed mat after hail .

children.text: Shingle pieces in the yard and fresh granules at the downspouts are clues. Granules also wash off as a roof ages, so they aren't proof on their own. Hail bruises rarely show from the ground, which is why Roof King photographs every slope, not just the side facing the street .

cards.title: Edges, flashing and vents
cards.description: Roof edges, ridges and the flashing at walls, chimneys and pipes are where wind gets a grip.

children.text: Look for bent or lifted metal at the roof edge, flashing pulled away from a wall or chimney, and dented or cracked vent caps. Roof King inspects flashing, penetrations, valleys and transitions one by one .

cards.title: Attic and ceilings
cards.description: New stains, damp insulation or daylight through the roof boards mean water or debris got through.

children.text: Look only from the attic hatch with a flashlight, and don't step between joists. Roof King checks the attic where there's access, for moisture and ventilation .

cards.title: Gutters and downspouts
cards.description: Dents, pulled hangers and sagging runs are common after hail and wind.

children.text: A dented gutter tells you hail fell. It doesn't, by itself, mean the shingles need replacing . Gutter, fascia and other soft-metal damage gets recorded separately during the inspection . See
gutter services

cards.title: Siding and trim
cards.description: Look for cracked, punctured or missing panels and dented trim, usually worst on the side that faced the storm.

children.text: Siding and trim damage should get its own lines on the estimate, separate from the roof. See
siding services

cards.title: Windows and screens
cards.description: Torn screens, cracked glass and dented frames or wraps.

children.text: Watch for new drafts or leaks around a window in the days after a storm. See
window replacement

image.alt: Illustration of step flashing where shingles meet a brick chimney

items.caption: Illustration: roof-to-wall connections need their own assessment.

items.title: Hail vs wind damage

children.text: The National Weather Service treats a thunderstorm as severe when it brings winds of 58 mph or more, hail 1 inch across or larger, or both . Smaller storms can still damage a worn roof, and a severe storm doesn't guarantee damage. Hail and wind also leave different patterns.
NWS Severe Thunderstorm Criteria

items.description: The National Weather Service treats a thunderstorm as severe when it brings winds of 58 mph or more, hail 1 inch across or larger, or both . Smaller storms can still damage a worn roof, and a severe storm doesn't guarantee damage. Hail and wind also leave different patterns.
items.label: Explore Storm Damage Documentation

cards.title: Hail damage
cards.description: Impact marks scattered across a slope: bruises, cracks, missing granules and dents in soft metal.

children.text: Damage can vary slope by slope, so the inspection marks and documents test squares on each slope where hail is suspected . Vents, gutters and flashing are recorded on their own, because a dent in metal doesn't prove the shingles are damaged . More on the
hail damage roof repair
page .

cards.title: Wind damage
cards.description: Wind damage starts at edges, ridges and corners and shows up as missing, lifted or creased shingles.

children.text: A shingle can lift, crease and lose its seal without blowing off, so the courses around a missing piece need checking too. Displaced flashing can open a gap at a wall or chimney . More on the
wind damage roof repair
page , and in
why fall gusts over 40 mph matter

cards.title: Trees and large debris
cards.description: A falling limb can break roof boards, rafters and gutters, not just shingles.

children.text: Have the tree removed by a tree professional before any roof work, and stay out of rooms below until the structure is checked . One customer's tree-damage job ended with new roofs and gutters on two homes .

cards.title: GAF Timberline AS II
cards.description: Wind resistance: ASTM D7158 Class H: 150 mph; ASTM D3161 Class F: 110 mph. Impact resistance: UL 2218 Class 4 — 2-inch steel ball dropped 20 feet

children.text: Manufacturer-stated classification speeds under controlled laboratory conditions. Actual roof performance depends on roof design, exposure and installation; this is not a guaranteed storm speed or wind warranty.

items.question: Should I call my insurance company or a roofer first?

children.text: You can do both. Report the damage to your insurer promptly, because policies can have reporting deadlines . A Roof King inspection gives you written findings to share. Calling us does not start a claim .

items.question: What if I can't see any damage from the ground?

children.text: That's common with hail. Bruised shingles and lifted tabs rarely show from the yard. Tell us the storm date and any new leaks or stains, and stay off the roof. The inspection covers every slope .

items.question: Will Roof King deal with my insurance company for me?

children.text: No. In Ohio, negotiating or settling a property claim for a homeowner, for pay, is the work of a certified public insurance adjuster . Roof King provides the inspection photos, findings and estimate and explains them. You deal with your insurer .

items.question: Does storm damage mean I need a new roof?

children.text: Not necessarily. Isolated damage on a sound roof can often be repaired. Widespread damage, or shingles too worn to take a repair, points to replacement. The findings should show which applies.

items.question: Is the storm damage inspection free?

children.text: Yes. It's free with no obligation, and you keep the documented findings whether or not you hire Roof King .

items.question: Can you tarp my roof if it's leaking?

children.text: Call (614) 379-8893 and describe where the water is coming in. Ask about temporary protection and inspection availability . A tarp is temporary, and the estimate will list the permanent repair separately.

items.question: Do I need a permit for storm damage roof repair in Columbus?

children.text: Replacing a roof inside Columbus city limits requires a building permit, but not plan review, and historic districts may need extra approval . For a smaller repair, ask what your project needs. Get your storm damage inspected

Drainage and adjoining exterior areas

Debris and damaged components can affect drainage. Record conditions at relevant drains, scuppers or gutters and note any related wall or cladding damage. A roofing proposal should identify the connections it addresses and the separate services still required.
Commercial storm repairs, replacement and recover suitability

A commercial roof repair may address an isolated damaged detail in a serviceable system. Wider damage or underlying deterioration may require a replacement assessment. A coating or recover method should not be assumed appropriate simply because it covers the visible surface. The recommendation needs evidence from the assembly and its condition.
Coordinating temporary protection and permanent commercial repairs

Confirm the decision-maker, access arrangements, staging, delivery hours and communication with occupants. Rooftop equipment and interior areas may require separate contractors or protection. Record temporary work and permanent work as distinct estimates, with a clear explanation of what remains to be done. Avoid assuming a temporary measure restores the roof's full service condition.
Commercial storm estimates, approved changes and completion records

Retain observations, photographs, estimates, authorized changes and completed-work records. The storm documentation page explains the construction record. Policy interpretation and coverage decisions belong with the insurer; a damage report or roofing estimate does not guarantee payment.
Mapping commercial storm observations to specific roof areas

Use a roof-area description or plan that connects photographs to specific locations. Record the affected material, observations, access limitations and proposed work. Keep reported interior damage separate from confirmed roof findings until the relationship is established. Earlier repairs and roof records help distinguish existing conditions from new observations.
Share the property address, roof information, storm observations and operating restrictions with Roof King. A useful repair plan connects the roof findings with the needs of the building below.
Can the business keep operating during repairs?
The answer depends on the building use, affected areas and required work. Discuss critical operations early so the proposal can identify practical arrangements and limitations.
What if hidden damage is found later?
The estimate should provide a way to document new findings, price the additional work and obtain authorization before covering the affected area.
Does a residential manufacturer credential cover all commercial systems?
No. Confirm qualifications and product requirements for the actual commercial assembly and proposed work.

items.title: Signs of hail damage

children.text: Real hail damage is random. Hits land scattered across a slope in different sizes, and the same storm marks the metal, siding and screens around the roof. A neat row of marks, or damage on one spot only, usually points to something else. Look from the ground or a window. Checking the roof surface is our job.

items.description: Real hail damage is random. Hits land scattered across a slope in different sizes, and the same storm marks the metal, siding and screens around the roof. A neat row of marks, or damage on one spot only, usually points to something else. Look from the ground or a window. Checking the roof surface is our job.
items.label: Discuss an Inspection

cards.title: Bruised shingles
cards.description: A hailstone can crush the asphalt and fiberglass mat under the granules without breaking the surface.

children.text: How a bruise shows up A dark, roughly round spot, often with granules pressed in or missing It gives slightly under a fingertip, like a soft spot on fruit. A blister doesn't. Bruises sit at random across the slope, more of them on the side that faced the storm They may not leak right away. The weakened spot can shed granules and crack later, which is why bruises are photographed and counted, not ignored.

cards.title: Granule loss
cards.description: Granules shield the asphalt from sun. Hail knocks them off in patches.

children.text: What granule loss does and doesn't prove Bare black spots on the shingle face, and heavy granules at downspout outlets after a storm Every roof sheds some granules with age, and new roofs shed loose ones in the first months. Granules in the gutter alone don't prove hail damage. What matters is exposed asphalt at impact points, matched to the storm date

cards.title: Cracks and mat fractures
cards.description: A hard hit can split the shingle and the fiberglass mat inside it.

children.text: Why fractures matter most A fracture is a break through the shingle. It can let water reach the underlayment. Fractures are hard to see from the ground and often show only when the shingle is lifted or flexed by hand The impact test behind Class 4 ratings fails a shingle when a crack shows on the back after two hits in the same spot, which is why fractures are treated as functional damage

cards.title: Soft metals on the roof
cards.description: Box vents, ridge vents, pipe flashing, valley metal, chimney caps and skylight curbs dent easily.

children.text: What dents tell us Dents show that hail hit and roughly how big it was, and which direction it came from A dented vent can be cosmetic, but a split or crushed one can leak Metal damage is recorded on its own line. A dented vent doesn't by itself mean the shingles failed.

cards.title: Gutters, downspouts and fascia
cards.description: Gutters often show the clearest hail marks on the house.

children.text: Cosmetic or functional Dents along the front lip and the top of downspout elbows A gutter that still holds its slope and drains is often cosmetic. Split seams, crushed sections or pulled hangers aren't. Gutter work is quoted separately and handled through our
gutter services

cards.title: Siding, window screens and sills
cards.description: Hail strong enough to damage a roof usually marks the walls, fences and cars nearby too.

children.text: Check the side that faced the storm Cracked or holed vinyl siding, chipped paint on wood or fiber cement, dented aluminum trim Torn or dented window screens and dented metal window wraps Spatter marks on decks, fences and outdoor equipment help date the storm Siding repairs go through our
siding services
; windows through
windows

cards.title: Damage that only looks like hail
cards.description: Several roof problems get mistaken for hail.

children.text: Look-alikes we rule out Blisters: raised or popped bubbles from trapped moisture or heat. No bruise underneath. Normal wear: even granule thinning across a whole slope, often worst on the south and west faces Foot traffic or tools: scuffs near walkways, ladders and the ridge Old repairs or manufacturing marks: patterns that repeat across the roof. Hail doesn't make patterns.

items.title: Hail size and your roof

children.text: Size isn't everything. Shingle type, age, wind and the angle of impact all change what a storm does. Still, size is the first thing an adjuster and a roofer ask about, so it helps to know the reference points.

groups.title: Hail size and your roof — Details

cards.title: What forecasters call severe hail
cards.description: NOAA's National Severe Storms Laboratory considers hail quarter size, 1 inch across, or larger to be severe.

children.text: Size comparisons Quarter: 1 inch, the severe threshold Half dollar: roughly 1¼ inches Size means the diameter of the hailstone.

cards.title: When shingles start to show damage
cards.description: Damage depends on the shingle and its condition, not just the storm.

children.text: What one state regulator advises homeowners The Nebraska Department of Insurance says hail generally needs to be about 1¼ inches across before it damages a roof. Lightweight composite shingles can show damage from 1-inch hail, and only deteriorated shingles are usually damaged by hail under 1 inch. An older, brittle roof can be damaged by hail a newer roof shrugs off, which is why we look at the roof's age and condition alongside the storm.

cards.title: Wind-driven hail
cards.description: Hail falling at an angle hits one side of the house harder.

children.text: Why one slope can look worse Slopes, walls and screens facing the storm take more and harder hits. Slopes on the far side can be untouched. We record each slope separately for that reason.

cards.title: Finding the storm date
cards.description: Your insurer will ask when the damage happened.

children.text: Where storm reports come from NOAA's Storm Events Database records hail where someone reported it, such as a trained spotter, a law-enforcement officer or a member of the public. A report a mile away doesn't prove your roof was hit, and no nearby report doesn't prove it wasn't. Hail falls in narrow, uneven bands. Your own dated photos of hail on the ground, dented cars or spatter marks are often the best record.

items.caption: Illustration: assess exposed metal separately from shingles.

items.title: Impact-resistant shingles (Class 4)

children.text: If hail means new shingles, it's worth looking at impact-rated lines. A UL 2218 Class 4 rating means samples survived a controlled test with a 2-inch steel ball. It's the highest class in that test. It doesn't make a roof hail-proof, and the rating describes new product in a lab.

items.description: If hail means new shingles, it's worth looking at impact-rated lines. A UL 2218 Class 4 rating means samples survived a controlled test with a 2-inch steel ball. It's the highest class in that test. It doesn't make a roof hail-proof, and the rating describes new product in a lab.
items.label: Discuss an Inspection

cards.title: How UL 2218 works
cards.description: Steel balls are dropped onto shingles. Each class uses a bigger ball.

children.text: Class 1 to Class 4 Each class uses a larger steel ball. Class 4, the highest, uses a 2-inch ball dropped from 20 feet. The steel-ball size isn't a guaranteed safe hailstone size. Real hail varies in shape, density and speed. A shingle passes if no crack is visible on the back after two impacts in the same spot. FM 4473 uses the same class sizes Manufacturers reach Class 4 with a reinforcing scrim on the back or with polymer-modified (rubberized) asphalt that flexes on impact

cards.title: The limits of a lab rating
cards.description: A rating is a fair starting point for comparing lines, not a promise.

children.text: What the test doesn't cover Standard impact tests don't account for weathering, temperature or aging. Ridge caps and accessories may not carry the same rating as the field shingle. Ratings apply to labeled packages, so the bundle on your roof should match the line on the proposal.

cards.title: IBHS ratings with lab-made hailstones
cards.description: The Insurance Institute for Business & Home Safety rates impact-resistant shingles with lab-made hailstones instead of steel balls.

children.text: How to use them IBHS grades shingles Excellent, Good, Marginal or Poor on dents, tears and granule loss. Its most recent ratings were released on November 19, 2025. Ask us to check where a line you're considering stands on the current list.

cards.title: Class 4 and your insurance
cards.description: Some insurers give a premium credit for impact-rated roofs. Others don't, or change their terms.

children.text: What to ask your insurer Whether your policy offers a credit for a Class 4 roof, and what proof it needs (product name and installation paperwork) Whether the credit changes your deductible or how cosmetic damage is covered We give you the product documentation. We can't promise a discount.

children.text: Why your roofer shouldn't negotiate your settlement Ohio law defines a public insurance adjuster as anyone who, for compensation, acts for or helps an insured negotiate or settle a property claim, or advertises that service. No one may act as one without a certificate of authority from the state's superintendent of insurance. Roof King is a roofing contractor. We don't negotiate settlements or act as your adjuster. If you want someone to represent you, ask the Ohio Department of Insurance about licensed public adjusters. Be cautious of anyone who offers to "handle everything" with your insurer in exchange for signing a contract.

faq.title: Hail Damage Roof Repair Questions

items.question: What size hail damages a roof?

children.text: NOAA's severe-storm lab treats hail 1 inch across (quarter size) or larger as severe. Whether it damages your roof depends on the shingles and their age. The Nebraska Department of Insurance says damage generally starts around 1¼ inches, lightweight shingles can be damaged by 1-inch hail, and older, deteriorated shingles by smaller stones. An inspection settles it for your roof.

items.question: Can a roof have hail damage without leaking?

children.text: Yes. Bruises and small fractures often don't leak at first. They weaken the shingle so it loses granules and cracks over time. That's why we record and count hits after a storm instead of waiting for a stain on the ceiling. See the "Signs of hail damage" tab above.

items.question: Will Roof King handle my insurance claim?

children.text: No. You file the claim and talk with your insurer, and your insurer decides coverage and payment. We inspect the roof, document the damage and explain our findings and estimate so you can share them. We speak with your insurer only if you ask us to and we agree on it first. In Ohio, negotiating a claim settlement for pay is reserved for licensed public insurance adjusters. More on
storm damage documentation

items.question: Does a hail inspection cost anything?

children.text: No. Our inspection is no cost and no obligation, and you get written findings with photos whether or not you hire us. It typically takes 45 to 90 minutes, depending on the size and complexity of the roof.

items.question: Do Class 4 shingles lower my insurance premium?

children.text: Some insurers offer a credit for impact-rated roofs and some don't, so ask your insurer what it offers and what proof it needs. We can give you the product name and the documents from your project. Class 4 means a shingle passed the UL 2218 test with a 2-inch steel ball. It doesn't make a roof hail-proof. See the Class 4 lines in the tab above.

items.question: Does a dented gutter mean my roof needs replacing?

children.text: Not by itself. Gutters and vents dent more easily than shingles, so dents show that hail hit, not that the shingles failed. We check the shingles on their own and list gutters separately. A gutter that still holds its slope and drains is often a cosmetic repair.

items.question: Do I need a permit to replace a hail-damaged roof in Columbus?

children.text: Yes, inside city limits. The City of Columbus requires a building permit, without plan review, to replace a roof. Historic and special zoning districts such as German Village may need extra approvals, and suburbs set their own rules.

items.question: What if the roof is leaking now?

children.text: Call

, tell us where water is showing and when the storm hit, and ask about current availability. Until then, catch the water, move belongings and stay off the roof. Keep receipts for anything you do to protect the house. Temporary protection and the permanent repair are separate steps. See
storm damage repairs

expectedBlocks: Hail can leave soft bruises in shingles, bare spots where granules were knocked loose, and dents in vents, gutters and flashing. Some damage can leak later and some is cosmetic. Roof King & Restoration handles hail damage roof repair in Columbus by checking the slopes and the soft metals around them. We photograph what we find and explain whether a repair, a section or a new roof makes sense. You decide what to take to your insurer.
Water coming in now? Call (614) 379-8893, describe the active problem and ask about current availability.
Choose what you want to understand: damage signs, hail size, impact-rated shingles, documentation or the repair decision.

Real hail damage is random. Hits land scattered across a slope in different sizes, and the same storm marks the metal, siding and screens around the roof. A neat row of marks, or damage on one spot only, usually points to something else. Look from the ground or a window. Checking the roof surface is our job.

How a bruise shows up A dark, roughly round spot, often with granules pressed in or missing It gives slightly under a fingertip, like a soft spot on fruit. A blister doesn't. Bruises sit at random across the slope, more of them on the side that faced the storm They may not leak right away. The weakened spot can shed granules and crack later, which is why bruises are photographed and counted, not ignored.

What granule loss does and doesn't prove Bare black spots on the shingle face, and heavy granules at downspout outlets after a storm Every roof sheds some granules with age, and new roofs shed loose ones in the first months. Granules in the gutter alone don't prove hail damage. What matters is exposed asphalt at impact points, matched to the storm date

Why fractures matter most A fracture is a break through the shingle. It can let water reach the underlayment. Fractures are hard to see from the ground and often show only when the shingle is lifted or flexed by hand The impact test behind Class 4 ratings fails a shingle when a crack shows on the back after two hits in the same spot, which is why fractures are treated as functional damage

What dents tell us Dents show that hail hit and roughly how big it was, and which direction it came from A dented vent can be cosmetic, but a split or crushed one can leak Metal damage is recorded on its own line. A dented vent doesn't by itself mean the shingles failed.

Cosmetic or functional Dents along the front lip and the top of downspout elbows A gutter that still holds its slope and drains is often cosmetic. Split seams, crushed sections or pulled hangers aren't. Gutter work is quoted separately and handled through ourgutter services

Check the side that faced the storm Cracked or holed vinyl siding, chipped paint on wood or fiber cement, dented aluminum trim Torn or dented window screens and dented metal window wraps Spatter marks on decks, fences and outdoor equipment help date the storm Siding repairs go through oursiding services ; windows throughwindows

Look-alikes we rule out Blisters: raised or popped bubbles from trapped moisture or heat. No bruise underneath. Normal wear: even granule thinning across a whole slope, often worst on the south and west faces Foot traffic or tools: scuffs near walkways, ladders and the ridge Old repairs or manufacturing marks: patterns that repeat across the roof. Hail doesn't make patterns.

Size isn't everything. Shingle type, age, wind and the angle of impact all change what a storm does. Still, size is the first thing an adjuster and a roofer ask about, so it helps to know the reference points.
Size comparisons Quarter: 1 inch, the severe threshold Half dollar: roughly 1¼ inches Size means the diameter of the hailstone.

What one state regulator advises homeowners The Nebraska Department of Insurance says hail generally needs to be about 1¼ inches across before it damages a roof. Lightweight composite shingles can show damage from 1-inch hail, and only deteriorated shingles are usually damaged by hail under 1 inch. An older, brittle roof can be damaged by hail a newer roof shrugs off, which is why we look at the roof's age and condition alongside the storm.
Why one slope can look worse Slopes, walls and screens facing the storm take more and harder hits. Slopes on the far side can be untouched. We record each slope separately for that reason.

Where storm reports come from NOAA's Storm Events Database records hail where someone reported it, such as a trained spotter, a law-enforcement officer or a member of the public. A report a mile away doesn't prove your roof was hit, and no nearby report doesn't prove it wasn't. Hail falls in narrow, uneven bands. Your own dated photos of hail on the ground, dented cars or spatter marks are often the best record.

If hail means new shingles, it's worth looking at impact-rated lines. A UL 2218 Class 4 rating means samples survived a controlled test with a 2-inch steel ball. It's the highest class in that test. It doesn't make a roof hail-proof, and the rating describes new product in a lab.

Class 1 to Class 4 Each class uses a larger steel ball. Class 4, the highest, uses a 2-inch ball dropped from 20 feet. The steel-ball size isn't a guaranteed safe hailstone size. Real hail varies in shape, density and speed. A shingle passes if no crack is visible on the back after two impacts in the same spot. FM 4473 uses the same class sizes Manufacturers reach Class 4 with a reinforcing scrim on the back or with polymer-modified (rubberized) asphalt that flexes on impact

What the test doesn't cover Standard impact tests don't account for weathering, temperature or aging. Ridge caps and accessories may not carry the same rating as the field shingle. Ratings apply to labeled packages, so the bundle on your roof should match the line on the proposal.

How to use them IBHS grades shingles Excellent, Good, Marginal or Poor on dents, tears and granule loss. Its most recent ratings were released on November 19, 2025. Ask us to check where a line you're considering stands on the current list.

What to ask your insurer Whether your policy offers a credit for a Class 4 roof, and what proof it needs (product name and installation paperwork) Whether the credit changes your deductible or how cosmetic damage is covered We give you the product documentation. We can't promise a discount./products/roofing/shingles/gaf/timberline-uhdz/

A hail claim is between you and your insurer. We inspect the roof, record what we find and explain the repair estimate so you have clear construction facts to share. Your insurer reviews the claim under your policy and decides coverage and payment.

Roles in a hail claim You report the claim to your insurer, share the records you choose and authorize the work Your insurer inspects through its own adjuster, reviews the claim under the policy and decides coverage and payment Roof King inspects, documents and explains the construction findings and the estimate. If you want us to speak with your insurer, that's agreed with you in writing first.

Why your roofer shouldn't negotiate your settlement Ohio law defines a public insurance adjuster as anyone who, for compensation, acts for or helps an insured negotiate or settle a property claim, or advertises that service. No one may act as one without a certificate of authority from the state's superintendent of insurance. Roof King is a roofing contractor. We don't negotiate settlements or act as your adjuster. If you want someone to represent you, ask the Ohio Department of Insurance about licensed public adjusters. Be cautious of anyone who offers to "handle everything" with your insurer in exchange for signing a contract.

Check your policy Look for the reporting period and any limits on cosmetic damage to roofs or metal. If you're unsure, ask your agent or insurer before the deadline passes. A dated inspection record helps either way.

What each warranty covers GAF's warranties don't cover hail damage as a manufacturing defect, and System Plus doesn't replace storm-damage insurance. Under Roof King's workmanship warranty, storm damage is reviewed under its own applicable terms.

Hail doesn't automatically mean a new roof. The decision comes from how many slopes are damaged, how badly, the roof's age and whether new shingles can be blended in. When the findings point to replacement, we show why. The full replacement guide is onroof replacement .

Signs a repair stops making sense Bruises or fractures on most slopes Widespread granule loss at impact points A brittle, older roof that cracks when shingles are lifted for a repair A discontinued line that can't be matched on a visible slope

What to expect Weathering changes color, and lines get discontinued. We show you the closest available match before work starts, and we're honest when a patch would stand out. Whether insurance pays for matching is a policy question for your insurer.

cards.title: Stay safe and stay off the roof
cards.description: Wind-damaged roofs are slick, loose and sometimes carrying limbs or wires.

children.text: Before anything else Call 911 for downed power lines, a structural collapse or fire. If you smell gas, leave the house and call Columbia Gas at 1- 800-282-7820 from outside. Stay out of rooms or buildings with visible structural damage until a professional has checked them. Look and photograph from the ground or from inside. Don't climb up or pull at loose shingles, flashing or limbs.

cards.title: Slow the water down
cards.description: Temporary protection buys time. It isn't the repair.

children.text: What temporary protection does and doesn't do Inside: move belongings, catch drips and start drying wet materials. The City of Columbus advises starting within 24 to 48 hours to limit mold. On the roof: a temporary cover over an opening is installed where it's appropriate and available. Call (614) 379-8893 and describe the problem so availability can be discussed. Keep receipts for emergency supplies, temporary repairs and professional services. Temporary protection doesn't seal broken shingle bonds or reattach flashing. The estimate should say what it covers and what permanent work remains.

cards.title: Record it before cleanup
cards.description: Photos taken the day of the storm are the best record you'll have.

children.text: What to record Photos and video of every damaged area inside and out, with the date and time Shingles, ridge pieces, flashing or gutter sections in the yard. Photograph them where they landed and keep them. Ceiling stains, drips and attic wetness Don't throw away damaged items until your insurance carrier says it's acceptable. Our
storm documentation page
explains how inspection photos, the estimate and completed-work records fit together.
